1 Pre-COVID and Post-COVID Exploratory Data Analysis

2 Setup

2.1 Plot Colors and Theme

# Define consistent colors and identify the variables used throughout the comparisons.
pre_color <- "#377EB8"
post_color <- "#E69F00"

phq_color <- "#377EB8"
gad_color <- "#E69F00"

gender_colors <- c(
  "Men" = "#377EB8",
  "Women" = "#E69F00"
)

period_colors <- c(
  "2017-2018 Pre-COVID" = "#377EB8",
  "2022-2023 Post-COVID" = "#E69F00"
)

measure_colors <- c(
  "PHQ" = "#377EB8",
  "GAD" = "#E69F00"
)

theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
      axis.text.x = element_text(
        angle = 0,
        hjust = 0.5
      ),
      legend.position = "bottom",
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )
)

3 Load Data

# Load the cleaned pre-COVID and post-COVID datasets from the project folders.
project_root <- here::here()

pre_path <- file.path(project_root, "data", "processed", "pre_covid_clean.csv")
post_path <- file.path(project_root, "data", "processed", "post_covid_clean.csv")

# Confirm the project root and both input files.
if (!file.exists(pre_path) || !file.exists(post_path)) {
  stop(
    "Missing processed data files. Open the project's .Rproj file first. ",
    "Project root: ", project_root, ". ",
    "Expected: data/processed/pre_covid_clean.csv and ",
    "data/processed/post_covid_clean.csv"
  )
}

pre_covid <- readr::read_csv(pre_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
post_covid <- readr::read_csv(post_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

# Confirm the variables used throughout the descriptive analysis.
variables_used <- c(
  "PHQ", "GAD", "gender", "field", "race.2", "yr_sch.2", "fincur.2", "age"
)

for (period_name in c("pre_covid", "post_covid")) {
  missing_columns <- setdiff(variables_used, names(get(period_name)))
  if (length(missing_columns) > 0) {
    stop(period_name, " is missing: ", paste(missing_columns, collapse = ", "))
  }
}

4 Make Variables Consistent

# Standardize the post-COVID variable categories so they can be compared with the pre-COVID data.
post_covid <- post_covid %>%
  mutate(
    field = case_when(
      as.character(field) == "STEM" ~ "STEM",
      as.character(field) %in% c("NotSTEM", "Non-STEM") ~ "Non-STEM",
      TRUE ~ as.character(field)
    ),
    gender = as.character(gender),
    field = as.character(field),
    race.2 = as.character(race.2),
    yr_sch.2 = as.character(yr_sch.2),
    fincur.2 = as.numeric(fincur.2),
    age = as.numeric(age)
  )

pre_covid <- pre_covid %>%
  mutate(
    gender = as.character(gender),
    field = as.character(field),
    race.2 = as.character(race.2),
    yr_sch.2 = as.character(yr_sch.2),
    fincur.2 = as.numeric(fincur.2),
    age = as.numeric(age)
  )

pre_covid$gender <- factor(
  pre_covid$gender,
  levels = c("Men", "Women")
)

post_covid$gender <- factor(
  post_covid$gender,
  levels = c("Men", "Women")
)

pre_covid$field <- factor(
  pre_covid$field,
  levels = c("Non-STEM", "STEM")
)

post_covid$field <- factor(
  post_covid$field,
  levels = c("Non-STEM", "STEM")
)

race_levels <- c(
  "White",
  "Asian",
  "Black",
  "Hispanic",
  "Middle Eastern"
)

pre_covid$race.2 <- factor(
  pre_covid$race.2,
  levels = race_levels
)

post_covid$race.2 <- factor(
  post_covid$race.2,
  levels = race_levels
)

year_levels <- c(
  "firstyear",
  "secondyear",
  "thirdyear",
  "fourthyear+"
)

pre_covid$yr_sch.2 <- factor(
  pre_covid$yr_sch.2,
  levels = year_levels
)

post_covid$yr_sch.2 <- factor(
  post_covid$yr_sch.2,
  levels = year_levels
)

5 Final Data Check

# Check the number of observations and variables in the pre-COVID dataset.
dim(pre_covid)
## [1] 68427    29
# Check the number of observations and variables in the post-COVID dataset.
dim(post_covid)
## [1] 43910    31
# Confirm that the variables needed for descriptive analysis exist in both datasets.
# Verify that both datasets contain the analysis variables.
variable_check <- data.frame(
  Variable = variables_used,
  Pre_COVID = variables_used %in% names(pre_covid),
  Post_COVID = variables_used %in% names(post_covid)
)

knitr::kable(
  variable_check,
  caption = "Variables Available in Both Datasets"
)

6.2 Missing Values

# Count missing values for each selected variable in the pre-COVID sample.
pre_missing <- data.frame(
  Variable = variables_used,
  Missing = sapply(
    pre_covid[, variables_used],
    function(x) sum(is.na(x))
  ),
  Percent_Missing = sapply(
    pre_covid[, variables_used],
    function(x) mean(is.na(x)) * 100
  )
)

pre_missing$Percent_Missing <- round(
  pre_missing$Percent_Missing,
  2
)

knitr::kable(
  pre_missing,
  caption = "Missing Data: 2017-2018"
)

6.3 Depression and Anxiety Scores

# Summarize the distribution of pre-COVID depression (PHQ) scores.
summary(pre_covid$PHQ)
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.    NA's 
##   1.000   1.333   1.778   1.892   2.222   4.000   16788
# Summarize the distribution of pre-COVID anxiety (GAD) scores.
summary(pre_covid$GAD)
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.    NA's 
##   1.000   1.286   1.857   1.984   2.429   4.000   17362
# Plot the distribution of depression scores in the pre-COVID sample.
ggplot(pre_covid, aes(x = PHQ)) +
  geom_histogram(
    binwidth = 1/9,
    fill = phq_color,
    color = "white"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Depression Scores: 2017-2018",
    x = "PHQ Score",
    y = "Students"
  )

Most students had lower depression scores, with fewer students having scores toward the higher end of the scale.

# Plot the distribution of anxiety scores in the pre-COVID sample.
ggplot(pre_covid, aes(x = GAD)) +
  geom_histogram(
    binwidth = 1/7,
    fill = gad_color,
    color = "white"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Anxiety Scores: 2017-2018",
    x = "GAD Score",
    y = "Students"
  )

Most students had lower anxiety scores, although there were still students with scores across the full range.

6.4 Gender Distribution

# Show the gender composition of the pre-COVID sample.
ggplot(
  filter(pre_covid, !is.na(gender)),
  aes(x = gender, fill = gender)
) +
  geom_bar() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = gender_colors) +
  guides(fill = "none") +
  labs(
    title = "Gender Distribution: 2017-2018",
    x = "Gender",
    y = "Students"
  )

There were more women than men in the pre-COVID sample.

6.5 STEM and Non-STEM Distribution

# Show the distribution of STEM and non-STEM fields before COVID-19.
ggplot(
  filter(pre_covid, !is.na(field)),
  aes(x = field)
) +
  geom_bar(fill = pre_color) +
  labs(
    title = "STEM Status: 2017-2018",
    x = "Field",
    y = "Students"
  )

The pre-COVID sample included both STEM and non-STEM students, with more students in the non-STEM group.

6.6 Race Distribution

# Describe the racial composition of the pre-COVID sample.
ggplot(
  filter(pre_covid, !is.na(race.2)),
  aes(x = race.2)
) +
  geom_bar(fill = pre_color) +
  labs(
    title = "Race Distribution: 2017-2018",
    x = "Race",
    y = "Students"
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    labels = c(
      "White",
      "Asian",
      "Black",
      "Hispanic",
      "Middle\nEastern"
    )
  )

White students made up the largest racial group in the pre-COVID sample.

6.10 Mental Health by Gender

# Compare pre-COVID depression and anxiety scores across gender groups.
pre_gender_scores <- pre_covid %>%
  select(gender, PHQ, GAD) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    c(PHQ, GAD),
    names_to = "Measure",
    values_to = "Score"
  )

ggplot(
  filter(
    pre_gender_scores,
    !is.na(gender),
    !is.na(Score)
  ),
  aes(
    x = gender,
    y = Score,
    fill = gender
  )
) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_wrap(~Measure) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = gender_colors) +
  guides(fill = "none") +
  labs(
    title = "Mental Health Scores by Gender: 2017-2018",
    x = "Gender",
    y = "Score"
  )

Women generally had higher depression and anxiety scores than men before COVID.

6.15 Depression and Anxiety Relationship

# Calculate the correlation between pre-COVID depression and anxiety scores.
pre_correlation <- cor(
  pre_covid$PHQ,
  pre_covid$GAD,
  use = "complete.obs"
)

pre_correlation
## [1] 0.7497138
# Visualize the relationship between pre-COVID depression and anxiety scores.
ggplot(
  pre_covid,
  aes(x = PHQ, y = GAD)
) +
  geom_point(
    alpha = 0.08,
    color = pre_color
  ) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",
    se = FALSE,
    color = "black"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Depression and Anxiety: 2017-2018",
    x = "PHQ Score",
    y = "GAD Score"
  )

Depression and anxiety had a strong positive relationship, meaning students with higher depression scores also tended to have higher anxiety scores.

7.2 Missing Values

# Count missing values for each selected variable in the post-COVID sample.

  Variable = variables_used,
  Missing = sapply(
    post_covid[, variables_used],
    function(x) sum(is.na(x))
  ),
  Percent_Missing = sapply(
    post_covid[, variables_used],
    function(x) mean(is.na(x)) * 100
  )
)

post_missing$Percent_Missing <- round(
  post_missing$Percent_Missing,
  2
)

7.3 Depression and Anxiety Scores

# Summarize the distribution of post-COVID depression (PHQ) scores.
summary(post_covid$PHQ)
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.    NA's 
##   1.000   1.444   1.889   1.990   2.444   4.000    2441
# Summarize the distribution of post-COVID anxiety (GAD) scores.
summary(post_covid$GAD)
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.    NA's

# Plot the distribution of depression scores in the post-COVID sample.
ggplot(post_covid, aes(x = PHQ)) +
  geom_histogram(
    binwidth = 1/9,
    fill = phq_color,
    color = "white"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Depression Scores: 2022-2023",
    x = "PHQ Score",
    y = "Students"
  )

Most students had lower to moderate depression scores, although scores were spread across the full range.

# Calculate the correlation between post-COVID depression and anxiety scores.

post_correlation
## [1] 0.7419098
# Visualize the relationship between post-COVID depression and anxiety scores.
ggplot(
  post_covid,
  aes(x = PHQ, y = GAD)
) +
  geom_point(
    alpha = 0.08,
    color = post_color
  ) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",
    se = FALSE,
    color = "black"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Depression and Anxiety: 2022-2023",
    x = "PHQ Score",
    y = "GAD Score"
  )

Depression and anxiety had a strong positive relationship after COVID, so students with higher depression scores also tended to have higher anxiety scores.

8 Pre-COVID vs. Post-COVID Comparison

8.1 Create Combined Dataset

# Combine the two samples and label each observation by COVID period.
pre_compare <- pre_covid %>%
  select(all_of(variables_used)) %>%
  mutate(
    Period = "2017-2018 Pre-COVID"
  )

post_compare <- post_covid %>%
  select(all_of(variables_used)) %>%
  mutate(
    Period = "2022-2023 Post-COVID"
  )

combined <- bind_rows(
  pre_compare,
  post_compare
)

combined$Period <- factor(
  combined$Period,
  levels = c(
    "2017-2018 Pre-COVID",
    "2022-2023 Post-COVID"
  )
)

8.2 Sample Sizes

# Compare the total sample sizes for the pre-COVID and post-COVID periods.
combined %>%
  count(Period) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    caption = "Sample Size by Time Period"
  )
Sample Size by Time Period
Period n
2017-2018 Pre-COVID 68427
2022-2023 Post-COVID 43910

8.3 Missing Data Comparison

# Compare missing-data patterns across the two COVID periods.
missing_comparison <- combined %>%
  group_by(Period) %>%
  summarise(
    PHQ = mean(is.na(PHQ)) * 100,
    GAD = mean(is.na(GAD)) * 100,
    Gender = mean(is.na(gender)) * 100,
    Field = mean(is.na(field)) * 100,
    Race = mean(is.na(race.2)) * 100,
    Year = mean(is.na(yr_sch.2)) * 100,
    Financial_Stress = mean(is.na(fincur.2)) * 100,
    Age = mean(is.na(age)) * 100
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      where(is.numeric),
      ~ round(., 2)
    )
  )

knitr::kable(
  missing_comparison,
  caption = "Percent Missing by Time Period"
)

  aes(
    x = field,
    y = Mean_PHQ,
    fill = gender
  )
) +
  geom_col(
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
    width = 0.7
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~Period) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = gender_colors) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Depression by Gender and STEM Status",
    x = "Field",
    y = "Average PHQ Score",
    fill = "Gender"
  )

The gender difference in depression appears in both STEM and non-STEM students, with women generally having higher average depression scores than men.

10 Financial Stress and Mental Health Comparison

# Summarize mental health outcomes by financial circumstances and COVID period.
financial_summary <- combined %>%
  group_by(
    Period,
    fincur.2
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean_PHQ = mean(PHQ, na.rm = TRUE),
    Mean_GAD = mean(GAD, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    c(Mean_PHQ, Mean_GAD),
    names_to = "Measure",
    values_to = "Mean_Score"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Measure = recode(
      Measure,
      Mean_PHQ = "PHQ",
      Mean_GAD = "GAD"
    )
  )

ggplot(
  financial_summary,
  aes(
    x = fincur.2,
    y = Mean_Score,
    color = Period,
    group = Period
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~Measure) +
  scale_color_manual(values = period_colors) +
  labs(
    title = "Mental Health by Financial Stress Before and After COVID",
    x = "Financial Stress",
    y = "Average Score",
    color = "Time Period"
  )

Higher financial stress was associated with higher average depression and anxiety scores in both time periods.

13 Depression and Anxiety Correlation Comparison

# Compare the depression-anxiety correlation before and after COVID-19.
correlation_summary <- combined %>%
  group_by(Period) %>%
  summarise(
    PHQ_GAD_Correlation = cor(
      PHQ,
      GAD,
      use = "complete.obs"
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    PHQ_GAD_Correlation = round(
      PHQ_GAD_Correlation,
      3
    )
  )

knitr::kable(
  correlation_summary,
  caption = "Correlation Between Depression and Anxiety"
)
Correlation Between Depression and Anxiety
Period PHQ_GAD_Correlation
2017-2018 Pre-COVID 0.750
2022-2023 Post-COVID 0.742

The relationship between depression and anxiety stayed almost the same across the two time periods, with correlations of 0.75 before COVID and 0.74 after COVID.

14 Final EDA Summary

# Create a final descriptive summary of the two samples and their mental health outcomes.
eda_summary <- combined %>%
  group_by(Period) %>%
  summarise(
    Students = n(),
    PHQ_N = sum(!is.na(PHQ)),
    Mean_PHQ = mean(PHQ, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median_PHQ = median(PHQ, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_PHQ = sd(PHQ, na.rm = TRUE),
    GAD_N = sum(!is.na(GAD)),
    Mean_GAD = mean(GAD, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median_GAD = median(GAD, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_GAD = sd(GAD, na.rm = TRUE),
    Mean_Age = mean(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    Mean_Financial_Stress = mean(
      fincur.2,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    PHQ_GAD_Correlation = cor(
      PHQ,
      GAD,
      use = "complete.obs"
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      where(is.numeric),
      ~ round(., 2)
    )
  )

knitr::kable(
  eda_summary,
  caption = "Overall EDA Summary"
)
Overall EDA Summary
Period Students PHQ_N Mean_PHQ Median_PHQ SD_PHQ GAD_N Mean_GAD Median_GAD SD_GAD Mean_Age Mean_Financial_Stress PHQ_GAD_Correlation
2017-2018 Pre-COVID 68427 51639 1.89 1.78 0.67 51065 1.98 1.86 0.79 22.96 2.88 0.75
2022-2023 Post-COVID 43910 41469 1.99 1.89 0.70 41047 2.15 2.00 0.83 20.97 3.13 0.74

Overall, both depression and anxiety scores were higher in the post-COVID sample, while the relationship between depression and anxiety remained very similar across the two time periods.

15 EDA Conclusions

The exploratory analysis above allows us to compare the characteristics of the 2017-2018 and 2022-2023 samples before fitting statistical models.

The main outcomes of interest are depression and anxiety scores. Gender and STEM status are the main groups of interest, while age, race, year in school, and financial stress are also examined because they will be considered in the later modeling.

The next step will be to split the data into training, testing, and validation sets and begin the analytical modeling and validation stages of the data science pipeline.
